upsertPapers.title: Graph k-Coloring in Average Sublinear Time
upsertPapers.publicationEvidence: The author paper record states FOCS 2026.

upsertSlices.label: Average-input k-coloring · full output · zero error
upsertSlices.task: Output a proper coloring with colors from [k] for every promised k-colorable graph
assumptions: Input G is uniformly distributed over all labeled k-colorable graphs on [n] for the average complexity statement.
The algorithms must output a proper coloring on every promised graph, not merely with high probability over G.
Randomized average is E_{G∼U} E_r T(G,r); deterministic average is E_{G∼U} T(G).
One matrix-entry query costs constant time. Thus query count is bounded above by total runtime.
Internal failure triggers further stages and ultimately exhaustive search; external output is a full coloring, never FAIL.

results.bound: Randomized O(nk); deterministic Õ(nk) average runtime
results.guarantee: Proper full coloring with colors from [k], zero error on every promised input and random string
results.sourceLocation: Theorems 1–2; §1.1 matrix-access statement and §§5.2–5.3 correctness/runtime proofs
results.notes: These are average-input bounds, not worst-case runtime guarantees and not per-vertex LCA bounds. The tilde hides polylog(n); no particular logarithmic exponent is inferred. k is a colorability promise, not maximum degree or a claim that every color must be used. Zero error: every k-colorable input and every random string produce a proper full coloring. Runtime is averaged over the random input and, for the randomized algorithm, its coins. FAIL occurs only inside subroutines; exhaustive fallback completes the coloring. Validity: 2 ≤ k ≤ n^(1/37).

results.bound: Ω(nk) pair queries and time on every input; therefore also on average
results.guarantee: Proper full coloring with colors from [k], zero error on every promised input and random string
results.sourceLocation: Theorem 3; stronger Theorem 9 and matrix-query adversary proof in §6; §2.4 query statement
results.notes: This strengthens the original average-runtime wording. The proof directly bounds matrix queries and hence time. Its larger k-range is shown beyond the upper-bound range, without implying that this source supplies an algorithm there. The theorem also discusses unsorted-list access, but the figure restricts to matrix pair queries. No NP-hardness assumption is needed. Requires worst-case correctness: for every k-colorable input and every random string the algorithm outputs a proper full k-coloring. Applies to deterministic and zero-error randomized algorithms, not an unqualified bounded-error model. Validity: 2 ≤ k ≤ n^(1/3).
